CHROMIUM/HACK: drm/rockchip: add dual mipi support This is not the recommended binding upstream -- the suggestion there is to have both DSIs link to the same panel, mark one of them with a bool 'clock-master' property, and then do graph-traversal to determine there are two DSIs pointed to the same panel (and therefore should be used in paired mode). This has been having quite a few hiccups though, and this is "good enough" (in fact, a similar approach was used for the Nvidia Tegra DSI controller). Other deficiencies: * this relies on the two DSIs binding in the right order (this is guaranteed if we probe in the right order, I believe, since they get added to the display driver's lists in sequence) * there are probably corner cases if we unbind a DSI from the driver, since the master device tends to play with some of the slave device's internal structures. That probably should be revisited change-log: v1: fix some typo clear the dual mipi bit v2: test changed dtsi v3: remove slave mode in dw_mipi_dsi_get_lane_mbps move host_register return __dw_mipi_dsi_probe v4: really stop using 'drvdata' in bridge driver add helper for mode-setting the master and slave stop parsing 'rockchip,dual-channel' in bridge driver fix up some error handling BUG=b:65001779 TEST=show ui when boot scarlet rev0 & rev1 Change-Id: I5be3b10a6ff52338a374ebe600445c14ecdbe304 Signed-off-by: Nickey Yang <nickey.yang@rock-chips.com> Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/760451

tpm_utils: wait for attestation after clearing tpm owner Wait for both the attestation and tpm to be ready after clearing the tpm owner if wait_for_ready is requested. After the tpm is ready, prepare for enrollment is run. This takes a long time, and occupies cryptohome for a while. If you try to remove rootfs verification or use crypohome during this, it will fail. Wait for attestation to be prepared before returning, so we know prepare for enrollment is done and cryptohome can be used. BUG=none BRANCH=none TEST=run firmware_Cr50Update a bunch Change-Id: I26671b70c98d39f0dcdc0302336f61a9fa3d1490 Signed-off-by: Mary Ruthven <mruthven@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/802398 Reviewed-by: Aseda Aboagye <aaboagye@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: tpm: cr50_i2c: handle large burstcnt Before this change, when reading the response header, we always read burstcnt bytes and didn't check that the burstcnt is smaller than the provided buffer. If the chip returned garbage in burstcnt, we could read more than the provided buffer and corrupt the stack. This CL adds an extra check and fails the read operation, if the burstcnt is too large. BUG=b:67923075 BUG=b:68143437 TEST=introduce artificial error, check that we don't read if burstcnt is garbage and bigger than the buffer size. Signed-off-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Change-Id: I03e6bc50d6927c1baf9edf4f7868c876907b6fe3 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/765104 Commit-Ready: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Tested-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: tpm: cr50_i2c: better handling for large responses In case the header of the response indicates that it is larger than the provided buffer: 1) Print additional info in the error message, specifying the size of the response and the size of the buffer. 2) Return an error from the read function, instead of the incomplete response. BUG=b:68143437 TEST=introduce an artificial error, check driver behavior Signed-off-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Change-Id: I85c769d0e118359c1ff67789869f8883a02f4322 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/765105 Commit-Ready: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Tested-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com>

CHROMIUM: add internal cursor fb to fb list The legacy drm_mode_cursor / drm_mode_cursor2 ioctls end up creating an interal framebuffer. However, where this framebuffer should be freed is not immediately obvious, since the ioctls don't give userspace an handle to this internal fb. Let's add it to fb list, so drm_fb_release (called by drm_release) will close it. BUG=chromium:654131 TEST=After drm_cursor_test, internal fb is no longer seen via modetest This should help with graphics_Drm flakiness. Change-Id: Ie754f6f518f663bf7e308dd83ebf7f18f49a26bb Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/804665 Commit-Ready: Gurchetan Singh <gurchetansingh@chromium.org> Tested-by: Gurchetan Singh <gurchetansingh@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org>
